description_text: PRESOLICITATION NOTICE Request for Architect Services (A/E) 330 submission Solicitation: 36C25526R0136 Correct Structural Deficiencies Project No. 589A4-27-100 CONTRACT INFORMATION This A-E Services requirement is being procured in accordance with the Brooks Act (Public Law (PL0582) and implemented in accordance with the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Subpart 36. Firms will be selected for negotiation based on demonstrated competence and qualifications for the required work. This procurement is restricted to Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) firms. This requirement is being procured in accordance with the VAAR 836.606-71 as implemented in FAR Subpart 36.6. This is not a Request for Proposal, and an award will not be made with this announcement. This announcement is a request for SF 330 s from qualified Architectural and Engineer (A&E) contractors that meet the professional requirements. The selection criteria for this acquisition will be in accordance with FAR 36.602-1, evaluation factors are listed below. The completed SF 330 will be evaluated by the Columbia VAMC Evaluation Board in accordance with FAR 36.602-5(a) and the selection report shall serve as the final selection list, which will be provided directly to the Contracting Officer. Negotiations will be conducted beginning with the most highly qualified firm. The Government will not pay nor reimburse any costs associated with responding to this request. The Government is under no obligation to award a contract as a result of this announcement. The contract is anticipated to be awarded no later than August 2026. Award of any resultant contract is contingent upon the availability of funds. No solicitation document is available and no other information pertaining to project scope, etc. is available at this time. Any request for assistance with submission or other procedural matters shall be submitted to Jeanette Mathena and Kelsey Eagle via e-mail to: jeanette.mathena@va.gov and kelsey.eagle@va.gov. Personal visits to discuss this announcement will not be allowed. The NAICS Code for this procurement is 541310 A/E Services and the small business size standard of $12.5 Million. Award of a Firm Fixed Price contract is anticipated. Anticipated time for completion of design is estimated at 180 calendar days including time for VA reviews. The A/E firm shall also be required to perform construction services if award of a construction project contract is made. PROJECT INFORMATION This project corrects structural deficiencies related to securing mechanical equipment, piping and lighting. The facilities seismic risk category has changed from Low to Moderate Low. As a result, there are requirements for securing/bracing items in the facility that have not previously been done. This project will identify those areas and install the required supports/bracing. Plumbing Code, OSHA, etc.) - Physical Security Design Manual for VA Facilities Note: The above documents can be found at the following website: http://www.cfm.va.gov/TIL/ BACKGROUND AND DESCRIPTION OF THIS CONSTRUCTION PROJECT The focus of this project will correct structural deficiencies identified in project 589A4-19-800 Correct Seismic Deficiencies , excluding shear wall improvements that were outlined in said report. For this current project, the selected A/E will have 180 calendar days to identify, classify, and design remedies for critical structural deficiencies. This effort will be accomplished through both field investigations and review of prior evaluations. Building structural deficiencies are typically classified into Major and Minor levels based on their impact on safety, load-bearing capacity, and habitability. These deficiencies represent flaws in design, construction, current condition or materials that can lead to performance issues, including catastrophic failure, if not addressed. Major Structural Deficiencies: These are significant issues in key load-bearing components: Foundation Deficiencies: Include settling, sinking, or heaving of the foundation. Signs include large stair-step cracks in masonry, diagonal cracks, and doors/windows that stick or won't close. Framing/Load-Bearing Defects: Involve undersized framing members, missing hardware, or poor-quality work during construction. Material Degradation: The weakening of materials, such as rotting wood, rusting steel, or spalling concrete, often caused by water infiltration. Water Intrusion: A major, persistent cause of structural decline, leading to oxidation in steel, rot in wooden components, and weakening of concrete foundations. Overloading: Damage caused by loads exceeding the building's original design capacity. Minor Structural Deficiencies: These are small, localized flaws that do not immediately compromise the safety or structural integrity of the entire building. Examples include small cracks in plaster, minor surface corrosion, or uneven finishes. These should still be addressed to prevent them from becoming major issues over time. Common items include: Cracks: Diagonal cracks (wider than 1/4 inch) in foundations or walls, and horizontal cracks in masonry. Movement/Settlement: Sloping and uneven floors and walking surfaces, sagging roofs, and bulging/leaning walls. Gaps: Visible gaps where walls meet ceilings or floors, indicating significant shifting. Failed Components: Deteriorating brickwork, failed gutters causing water damage, and oxidizing steel surfaces. Inadequately secured overhead appurtenances, such as pipes and ducts. Inadequately secured free-standing appurtenances, such as racks and electrical gear. Common FboNotice causes of Structural Deficiencies typically arise from: Original Design Deficiencies: Incorrect structural plans, such as missing or undersized components. Original Construction Deficiency: Poor quality work, improper installation, and not building to code. Material Deficiencies: Using inferior materials, such as defective concrete or weak timber. Operational/Maintenance Deficiencies: Neglecting repairs, allowing water to damage components, or poor drainage around the foundation. This project will evaluate and plan appropriate repairs and/or modifications to all hospital structures, equipment, and appurtenances that need structural repairs and/or fortification. This project SPECIFICALLY EXCLUDES evaluations of the HSTVAMC Parking Structure. The seismic study referenced at the beginning of this section should become a first step for this effort. Much of that study focused on seismic protections related to installing structural shear walls within the hospital. For several reasons, the priority of those construction efforts was reduced in priority. However, the referenced report also refers to certain structural integrity improvements that will be applicable to this project. SITE INVESTIGATION A/E shall be responsible for conducting site visits for the purpose of data gathering investigation and documentation of all existing conditions. Perform such investigations as required to accurately verify all existing conditions. Do not rely solely upon "as built" drawings. VA personnel will help with investigating the project site where prior experience with equipment and utilities will produce an appreciable advantage. The A/E firm shall be responsible for site review of the existing facility to verify the owner's existing documents and as-built drawings. Any modifications that are required to be made because of the site review shall be communicated to the VA and corrected by the A/E firm. All site investigations shall be completed during the site investigation phase. SCHEMATIC The A/E shall do several visits (minimum of 3) to the facility to meet and discuss with the Integrated Project Team. An agreed to and solid schematic design is the foundation for a successful design. The first meeting will be to do an initial site visit and hear the needs, wants and desires of the VA FM staff. The second meeting will be to present initial project ideas in a Major/Minor format. Appropriate schematics with A/E providing their pros/cons to each will also be provided. This visit is to be a working visit with the A/E having the ability to make changes, display these visually and provide some immediate feedback. During this visit, the discussion of phasing needs to begin with the VA providing the priority areas The third meeting shall depict the schematic result from meeting two, also depicting the phasing plan. During this meeting final schematic and phasing shall be finalized and agreed to with the A/E providing a final schematic with phasing one week after this meeting. Mechanical, plumbing, electrical, and fire and safety systems must meet current codes and standards, including VA Standards. A/E shall plan for the following design and review meetings as part of the Scope of Work. Meetings itemized in this Supplement B as on-site below are required to be completed at HSTVMH. All other review meetings may be conducted utilizing a web-based meeting program. Notice to Proceed will be a teleconference between the Contracting Officer, COR and AE firm. This serves as the start of the project. The Initial Kickoff Meeting/Site Investigation will be held with the HSTMVH engineering staff. This meeting will be intended to provide onsite familiarization with the project. Kickoff meeting will be onsite with facility personnel. This will be a broad overview of the project, laying out perimeters and boundaries prior to meeting with the Integrated Project Team (IPT). Immediately following this kickoff meeting, there will be a meeting with the IPT. This meeting is to gather the desires from the IPT as to what they would like to see in the design, flow concerns, etc. During the IPT meeting the AE will determine the current workflow and utilize lean design principles to develop proposed schematic design options. Site investigation shall occur during this time frame as well. A summary of site investigation findings shall be provided to the VA at the end of site investigation. Schematic Design: Schematic Design (SD) has been split into three distinct parts SD1, SD2, & SD3. Each SD shall include a detailed efficiency review. SD1 (Schematic Design Part 1, Initial SD) AE shall provide three (3) distinct SD layouts for VA review based on meetings with the IPT. A brief written synopsis containing the pros and cons of each shall also be provided within 20 days of the initial meetings. The VA will conduct a review of the SD layouts with the IPT and provide the AE comments within 5 days of receiving SD1. An onsite meeting with the user group will occur to discuss the submission of SD1, provide feedback and hear issues/concerns. SD2 (Schematic Design Part 2) The AE will review the VA comments and submit two (2) revised SD layouts to the VA within 20 days of the user meeting as part of SD2. If VA comments from SD1 provide a clear design path, only a single design for SD2 is required. If a clear path forward was not determined during SD1, two separate revised designs shall be submitted as part of SD2. The requirement for one or two revised schematic designs will be indicated on the return of SD1 in the approval comments. The VA will review the new SD layouts for 5 days. A virtual meeting with the user group will occur to discuss the submission of SD2, provide feedback and hear issues/concerns. SD3 (Schematic Design Part 3, Final SD) The AE will make a final SD layout submission for VA approval within 20 days of the user meeting The VA will review for 5 days and a teleconference to discuss will be had. This teleconference shall, pending results of SD3, provide the final input and approval. The VA must provide SD approval prior to moving into any formal DD work. All submissions during this phase shall be digital (pdf, word, excel). ESTIMATE SUBMISSION REQUIREMENTS General - the A/E shall submit a construction cost estimate with the drawings at each project submission. This estimate shall show the cost of construction, which would be expected to be reflected by the construction contractors' bids, if the bids were submitted on the same date as the estimate. The level of detail for this estimate shall be consistent with the degree of completeness of the drawings being submitted. Simply stated, this means that if a construction element is shown, it must be priced; if it is shown in detail, it must be priced in detail. For detailed elements, "lump sum" or "allowance" figures will not be acceptable. Use of Forms - VA Form 10-6238, Estimate Worksheet: This form serves two purposes: (a) to show the division of cost between labor and material for each cost item; and (b) to extend the level of detail of an estimate beyond square foot cost summaries. The estimated costs shall include all labor, materials, mobilization, overhead, insurance, and applicable contractor markup. A/E may utilize their estimate worksheets if approved in advance by the VA. Contracting officer requirements - in addition to submissions to the COR, the A/E shall submit ALL construction cost estimates also to the Contracting Officer. This document will be used as the Independent Government Estimate (IGE) for construction period services.
